evidence: Screen-level arithmetic and one-dimensional radiative transfer on committed products. The gaseous absorption is ITU-R P.676-13 Annex 1 line by line, reproduced to 1e-12 against ITU-R Study Group 3's validation examples on Earth, then integrated through the atmosphere domain's prescribed moon_1.2atm column at 295 K with oxygen at Earth's partial pressure: a computed result for a prescribed clear-sky column, on line parameters fitted to Earth's air. Rain uses ITU-R P.838-3 with Earth's drop spectra, its rate scaled by the Moon's slower fall (an estimate). The ring's view is geometry on the held matched stack, circular rings at their layout radii and tilts. Receivers, beams, grid, faults and storage are sized from the products and labelled design guesses; nothing is simulated through time beyond sampling the lunar cycle and the libration of the ring plane.
reading_rule: Pairs are [low-cost end, high-cost end] of C' with the food blend as the domain synthesis gives them, unless labelled. Intake is the beam power arriving at receivers and crowns, which the synthesis counts as heat on the Moon; delivered power is what reaches the loads. Absorption in dB and as the share of the beam lost; elevations in degrees; heights in km above the column's surface (sea level) unless named; latitudes are lunar, with the north and south alike. Tile counts are of the fleet's 28 million tiles; times in hours unless named; storage in TWh of electricity delivered.

usable_elevation_deg.basis: beams planned from 30 degrees up, where the air takes about 11% at sea level against 6% overhead

beams_per_receiver.basis: three beams from different parts of the ring, each rated for half the load, switched make-before-break

receiver_side_km.basis: a flat-filled patch a few kilometres across, as the domain synthesis sizes the ground receivers

storage_days.basis: the critical loads carried through a fault across the whole ring for a week, after the 7-day fuel that Earth keeps for safety-related emergency power (US NRC Regulatory Guide 1.137)

tile_utilisation.basis: half a transmitting tile's rating in use on average

small_collector_share.basis: the variant with collectors over a tenth of each transmitting tile

transmitter.value: a sandwich of collector and phased array over a tile's clear face, sun-pointing collectors
transmitter.basis: each beam may use the whole aperture

tile_faults_per_year.basis: one whole-tile outage a decade per tile

fuel_cell.basis: electricity per unit of hydrogen's lower heating value

bridge_hours.basis: batteries carry the critical loads while hydrogen plant starts

critical_shares.basis: residents: ventilation, water and sewage pumps, refrigeration of food and medicine, safety lighting, communications and health care; sky control: towns drift with the wind and steer only to keep clear; water: all; cultures: the power-made food's living cultures kept alive at a tenth of their feed; lamps: the lamp-lit farms dark, with air and water kept moving; close computing: the millisecond control kept on the Moon; the towns' hydrogen remade and trips shed

dry_highland_height_km.basis: the dry highland cities on ground 4 km or more above the sea, at the low end of it

ground_loads_follow_people.basis: food plants, lamp farms and close computing at the cities

composition.value: the middle of each C' pair, with the ground's 4 billion

reef_above_town_km.basis: the synthesis's reefs 5-10 km above a town

lunar_fall.basis: attenuation with the water held, Earth's drop spectra

rain_cell.value: uniform at the storm's peak surface rate from the ground to its top or the 0 C level, as wide as the storm

circular_rings.value: the layout's forced eccentricities of 0.11-0.16 are left out; distances swing by that share about each orbit

absorption.model: ITU-R P.676-13 Annex 1, equations 1-9 (line by line) and 13-19b (slant paths), refractivity by ITU-R P.453; layers 10 cm thick at the receiver, thickening by e^(1/100), to the column top at 1 Pa

composition.rule: oxygen line strengths and the Debye term scaled by the oxygen mole fraction over Earth's 0.2095; widths kept as P.676 gives them for air at the total pressure

link.rule: the main figures take each beam from a tile drawn at random from the arc above the usable elevation; the best tiles take every beam from the highest tile in view, the floor of what the air takes

rain.model: ITU-R P.838-3 equations 1-5, circular polarization (tilt 45 degrees)

cloud_on_the_path.rule: the largest share of time the equatorial ring holds cloud at any height the path crosses, from the ecology work's sky bands

rain.lunar_fall_rule: at a sixth of the gravity raindrops fall about 2.9 times slower (CM1, V ~ g^((b+1)/3) with b = 0.8), so a lunar rain rate holds 2.9 times the water of the same rate on Earth; attenuation below 10 GHz goes with the water held, so P.838-3 is read at the Earth rate that holds the same water

grid.rule: receivers at the loads, the ground's intake spread as its people; poleward of the last band that always sees a usable tile, the loads take power by line when that loses less than their own low beams

exposure.rule: a patch flat-filled at the 1978 peak with edges blurred by a whole tile's spot; the closed ground runs out to where the beam falls below the public level

backup.rule: each receiver tied to two neighbours by lines rated for its whole load

single_tiles.after_one_loss: the other two beams carry the whole load at their rating
single_tiles.after_two_losses: the last beam carries half the load until a fresh beam is placed

food.rule: the cities hold about a month of food (first screen), so production stops while the living cultures are kept alive

polar.synthesis: the ring below the horizon within about 5 degrees of its plane's poles
polar.computed: the stack's tilted rings keep tiles above every horizon
